dossiers.title: Time, sequence, duration, and completion
dossiers.claim: Temporal errors across the work move events over before/after boundaries, turn preparation into completion, change an ongoing act into a finished period, or add durations the source never promises. Because White Album 2 builds causality through delayed calls, travel, deadlines, anniversaries, and separations, these are also plot and motivation errors.
dossiers.sourcePattern: Chronology is carried through aspect, relative time expressions, calendar offsets, duration nouns, and corrections such as 'two days ago—no, last night.' The selected cases depend on distinctions like week's beginning versus end, about-to-happen versus already happened, the coldest part of a day versus a year, and six months from now versus six months later.
dossiers.todokanaiEffect: Deadlines cross weekends, omens follow events they are supposed to precede, future weddings appear to have already arrived, and a temporary separation becomes 'never.' Even when the scene remains readable, its planning horizon, urgency, or emotional commitment changes.
dossiers.limits: English tense need not mirror Japanese aspect mechanically, and a scene may summarize time loosely. A finding requires an explicit sequence, duration, completion state, or future horizon to change. The counterexamples show exact long-term spans and a dated concert plan preserved without temporal drift.

examples.note: Chiaki is invoking who Haruki was two days ago—no, as recently as last night. The English instead makes last night the time when she might have raised the matter.
examples.japanese:
そんな二日前...
いや、昨夜までの俺を持ち出されても、
こいつの言いたいことなんか理解できるはずもない。
examples.todokanai: Even two days ago… no, even if she were to have brought this out last night, I probably wouldn't have been able to understand her then either.

examples.note: A final push toward an already established goal becomes the beginning of work toward that goal.
examples.japanese:
「さてと…三年ぶりに力もらったことだし、
あたしもラストスパート頑張るか」
examples.todokanai: "Well then… now that I've gained some strength for the first time in three years, maybe it's time I started working toward my own goal as well."

examples.note: The couple are preparing for a June wedding six months in the future; the English places them half a year later and breaks the epilogue chronology.
examples.japanese:
そして今、俺達は半年後のジューンブライドに向けて、
様々な準備や契約や打ち合わせに追われている。
examples.todokanai: And now, half a year later, we're signing contracts and making lots of different arrangements in regards to the June bride.

examples.note: It is already too late at night for Suzuki to still be teasing Haruki; the English says her period of teasing was over, although she continues.
examples.japanese:
大体、人をからかって遊んでる時間帯は
とっくに過ぎ去ってるのにこの人は…
examples.todokanai: For the most part, her time of ridiculing others was long over.

examples.note: An early dismissal is an omen that something bad is about to happen; the English says the bad event has already happened.
examples.japanese:
こんな『早い』時間に帰されるなんて、
何か良くないことが起こる前ぶれとしか…
examples.todokanai: To be told to go home this early… This is a warning sign to me that something bad has happened…

examples.note: The article check will be ready at the beginning of next week; the English moves it to the end of the week.
examples.japanese:
「あ、アンサンブルの記事チェックの件でしょうか？
それでしたら週明けには…」
examples.todokanai: "Ah, could it be about the article inspection at Ensemble? In that case, you can do so at the end of the week…"

examples.note: Haruki identifies the pre-dawn hour as the coldest part of the day; the English changes it to the coldest time of the year.
examples.japanese: 「だいたい今くらいが一番寒い時間帯だからな」
examples.todokanai: "This is the coldest time of the year, after all."

examples.note: Setsuna says Haruki did not forget Kazusa; the English turns this observed past fact into a permanent future inability to forget.
examples.japanese:
「ううん、幻想だった。
春希くんは決してかずさのことを忘れなかった」
examples.todokanai: "No, it's a delusion for sure. Haruki-kun will never be able to forget about Kazusa."

examples.note: Haruki's immediate 'don't come' becomes 'never come back,' turning a present separation into an explicit permanent ban.
examples.japanese: 「いや………来るな」
examples.todokanai: "No… Never come back."

examples.note: Haruki offers to take leave and spend relaxed time together; the English invents an entire week off.
examples.japanese:
「帰ったら、すぐに会いに行くから。
会社、休み取ってゆっくり過ごそう？」
examples.todokanai: "When I come back, I'll come to you right away… We can take time off from work and spend the week together."

examples.note: The exact planning relation survives: Kazusa's concert in Japan is confirmed for January 27 at Onjuku Arts and Culture Hall.
examples.japanese:
かずさの日本公演が決まった。
１月２７日に、ここ御宿芸術文化ホールで。
examples.todokanai: Kazusa's concert in Japan is confirmed. January 27th in the Onjuku Art and Culture Hall.

examples.note: Todokanai TL preserves the deliberate contrast between five years apart and the possibility of overcoming ten.
examples.japanese:
俺たちの間の五年なんて、ないも同然だった…
十年なら、平気で乗り越えてしまうかもしれない。
examples.todokanai: These past five years apart might as well not have happened… We might actually be able to overcome ten years with ease.

dossiers.title: Quantities, thresholds, and scale
dossiers.claim: Concrete quantities are repeatedly pushed across thresholds, multiplied, or assigned to the wrong unit. The resulting English changes admission odds, phone behavior, travel time, money, battery life, file size, print scale, and even the amount of time lovers have left together.
dossiers.sourcePattern: The Japanese uses digit-count expressions, interval phrases, counters, censored large numbers, and relative thresholds whose direction matters: under three digits, calls at one-hour intervals, one bar lost rather than one remaining, more than a hundred thousand rather than almost that amount, and fewer than eight hours left rather than eight hours already lost.
dossiers.todokanaiEffect: The errors inflate or diminish stakes and sometimes destroy the scene's inference. Five rings become five calls, one file tens of megabytes becomes dozens of files, a mostly professional wardrobe becomes half, and an initial print run of copies becomes multiple 'first editions.' The numbers may look like minor details, but they are often the mechanism by which characters reason.
dossiers.limits: Literal numerical matching is not required when English can preserve direction, scale, and comic force idiomatically. These findings cross a material boundary, change the unit counted, or alter order of magnitude. The counterexamples show a comic exact count and a nonliteral rating whose small upward adjustment survives.

examples.note: The remaining students fall below three digits—fewer than one hundred; the English says the number remains in the triple digits.
examples.japanese:
その中でも、他の大学に推薦の決まった強者や負け組、
就職を決めた社会人組を除くと、残るは三桁を切る。
examples.todokanai: This includes the ones who decided on other universities, be it because they're overachievers or underachievers, and the ones who have decided to go into employment. Take them away, and the leftover number of students would be in the triple digits.

examples.note: Several calls continue at roughly one-hour intervals; the English multiplies this into several calls every hour.
examples.japanese:
…その電話があってから後、
朝まで、依緒と武也からのコールが
一時間おきくらいに数件続いてる。
examples.todokanai: …After that, Io and Takeya kept calling me several times per hour until morning came.

examples.note: Pain measured in thousands is inflated to hundreds of thousands.
examples.japanese: 「何千倍も、苦しかったんだよ…っ」
examples.todokanai: "Hundreds of thousands times more painful…"

examples.note: The Paris-to-Strasbourg express journey is roughly two and a half hours; the English cuts it to two.
examples.japanese:
ここはフランス北東部の都市、ストラスブール。
パリから特急で２時間半くらい。
examples.todokanai: This is Strasbourg, a city located in the northeast of France. Taking a trip from Paris to here, even on an express train, would take approximately two hours.

examples.note: Haruki's battery has decreased by one notch; the English says only one bar remains and turns minor use into near depletion.
examples.japanese:
電車の中も、タクシーの中も、
ずっと無駄にライトを使い続けて、
とうとう電池が一目盛り減ってしまった。
examples.todokanai: After pointlessly keeping the brightness on within not only the train but also the taxi, my battery has depleted to the point where it only has one bar left remaining.

examples.note: Mari says her self-funded return cost far more than 100,000 yen; the English says it cost almost 100,000.
examples.japanese:
「会社の金じゃないんだぞ、
自費で帰ってきたんだぞ…
今度は１０万どころの騒ぎじゃなかったんだぞ…っ」
examples.todokanai: "I wasn't paid by the company for this, you know. I paid to come back here on my own… You know that I've spent almost 100000 yen just for this, right…?"

examples.note: The great majority of Haruki's clothes are work suits and shirts; the English reduces that dominant uniform to half.
examples.japanese:
最低限の家具と家電。
持ってる服は、大半が仕事用のスーツやワイシャツ。
examples.todokanai: The bare minimum for any home. And half the clothes I have are work clothes and dress shirts.

examples.note: Calls used to transfer to voicemail after about five rings; the English invents five separate calls.
examples.japanese:
さっきまでは、５コールくらいで
留守番電話に移行してたのに、
今はずっとコールが続いている。
examples.todokanai: My five calls earlier got transferred to voicemail, but now my call is continuing.

examples.note: One file tens of megabytes in size becomes a few dozen files and an invented download bar.
examples.japanese:
数十メガのファイルが
ディスクのアクセスランプとともに流れ込んでいく。
examples.todokanai: A few dozen files appear on my download bar.

examples.note: A censored number of ten-thousands of copies in the initial print run becomes tens of thousands of 'first editions.'
examples.japanese:
「待て、待て、待て！
全国の書店で売るんだぞ！？
初版○万部だぞ！？」
examples.todokanai: "Wait, wait, wait! This is going to be selling in bookstores all over the country, you know!? And tens of thousands of first editions, at that!"

examples.note: Fewer than eight hours remain in the day; the English says eight hours have already been lost, leaving a very different amount.
examples.japanese:
今年最後のメモリアルデーにもかかわらず、
俺たちに残された時間は、すでに八時間を切っていた。
examples.todokanai: Despite being the last commemorative day of the year, we had already lost eight precious hours of it.

examples.note: The exact school-wide joke survives: Takeya would need twenty-four girlfriends to have one in every class across all years.
examples.japanese:
「お前はクラスごとに女がいないと気が済まないのか？
全学年全クラス２４人の彼女を作る気か？」
examples.todokanai: "You won't be satisfied until you have a girl from every class? Do you plan to get 24 girlfriends across all years and classes?"

examples.note: The English rating is nonliteral, but it preserves the source's essential relation: Haruki may be only slightly above average.
examples.japanese:
「見直されたくなかったら、周囲と同化して埋没した方がよっぽど効果的だぞ」

「なにそれ？」

　―けれど、もしかしたらほんの少しだけ平均より上かもしれない。

　　七人並み、八人並みくらいは行ってるかもしれない。

「ほら、『不良が猫に餌やってた』とかいう落差による高評価がなくなるから、みんな普通に評価してくれるだろ？」

「あたしは誰にも評価されるつもりはない」

　―その証拠に、見とれたりはしないけれど、ずっと間近で見ていても苦にならない。

　　このまま見つめ続けていても、多分…
examples.todokanai:
"If you don't want people to reevaluate their opinion of you, just going along with the flow would work out better, you know."

"What are you saying?"

But, maybe he's just a tiny bit above average.

Maybe he's like a 5.5, or a 6, instead of just a 5.

"Look, that way people wouldn't be so impressed when you give a rare display of good conduct and evaluate you more normally, right?"

"I have no intention of letting anyone evaluate me."

As proof, I might not be captivated by him, but looking at him up this close isn't terrible, either.

dossiers.title: Uncertainty, alternatives, and unsupported certainty
dossiers.claim: Todokanai TL sometimes resolves a question the Japanese deliberately leaves open, replaces two possible readings with one invented feeling, weakens a categorical conclusion into a possibility, or promotes a conditional hope into fact. These shifts change not just information but how Haruki, Setsuna, and Kazusa understand themselves and one another.
dossiers.sourcePattern: The source marks epistemic limits through conditionals, paired alternatives, conjectural negatives, suspended clauses, quantity questions, and distinctions between a retrospective observation and a permanent prediction. Its emotional logic often depends on a character refusing certainty or, in a different scene, reaching a conclusion without hedging.
dossiers.todokanaiEffect: The English makes Haruki sure Kazusa included herself in thoughts he is explicitly questioning, turns his fragile hope that she can be happy with him into a confident promise, and changes Setsuna's report that Kazusa remained first into a prophecy that Setsuna can never become first. Elsewhere it hedges the very selfish choice Haruki states categorically.
dossiers.limits: English should not preserve every Japanese hedge as verbal clutter, and context can license a firmer sentence. A finding requires a material change in what is known, merely possible, conditional, or categorical. The counterexamples show a genuinely unspecified image and alternative future times that remain explicitly open.

examples.note: Haruki does not know whether the damaged bond is already repaired; the English turns that present uncertainty into doubt that it will ever be repairable.
examples.japanese: 壊れた絆が完全に修復したかどうかもわからない。
examples.todokanai: I don't know if we'll ever be able to truly restore the bond that we once destroyed.

examples.note: Setsuna considers two readings—lingering attachment or a premonition of final separation; the English replaces both with one invented feeling.
examples.japanese:
それが、未練を伴ったものでも、
別れの予感を漂わせたものでも、
怖くて自分からなかなか動けないだろうって。
examples.todokanai: It's because I fear the feeling I got during our parting, so it felt like I couldn't move forward.

examples.note: Haruki wonders whether Kazusa included herself in the things she imagined; the English asserts that she certainly did.
examples.japanese:
その時、かずさが思い浮かべた『色々』に、
かずさ自身は登場していたんだろうか。
examples.todokanai: I'm sure that this "a lot" includes Kazusa herself in Kazusa's mind.

examples.note: Haruki is uncertain how many school rules he is breaking, not whether he is breaking any; the English shifts the scope of uncertainty.
examples.japanese:
俺の、いくつの校則を違反しているか定かでない行為は、
とうとう、校内で然るべき責任を持つ人たちの
知ることとなり。
examples.todokanai: My actions, which may or may not be a violation of the school rules, are found out by the school staff.

examples.note: A deliberately suspended counterfactual—if the person making the sound was...—is completed with an unsupported claim about a beautiful melody.
examples.japanese: しかも、その音を奏でてたのが…だったのなら…
examples.todokanai: On top of that, it's because… she's the one who played that beautiful melody…

examples.note: Kazusa's circumstances are not even an obstacle to Haruki; the English says only that they are not the main issue and leaves them as a possible lesser obstacle.
examples.japanese:
いや、そもそもあいつの今の境遇なんか、
俺にとって障害にすらならなかった。
examples.todokanai: You could even say that her current circumstances didn't really end up being the main issue for me here.

examples.note: The partly empty hall could provisionally be seen as a calm start; the English reverses this into doubt that the concert will begin quietly.
examples.japanese:
それでも、チケット販売時の瞬殺ぶりから考えると、
今のところ落ち着いた滑り出しに見えないでもなかった。
examples.todokanai: But considering all the noise that was made when the tickets were still on sale, I doubt the beginning of the concert will be a quiet one.

examples.note: Haruki categorically says sharing the burden would prevent him from choosing Kazusa; 'might' hedges the selfish motive he explicitly owns.
examples.japanese:
「………もし三人で背負ったら、
俺はもう、二人のうちからかずさを選べなくなる」
examples.todokanai: "…If we shared the burden among the three of us, then… I might be unable to pick Kazusa anymore."

examples.note: Haruki says if Kazusa can be happy and smile beside him; the English converts both conditional hopes into confident predictions.
examples.japanese:
「あいつが俺の側にいることで
幸せになってくれるなら。
隣にいるときだけでも笑ってくれるなら…」
examples.todokanai: "By being with me, she'll be happy. She'll smile for me just by being next to me…"

examples.note: Setsuna says Kazusa remained Haruki's number one during the period described; the English turns this into a prophecy that Setsuna can never become first.
examples.japanese:
「それでも、彼の中の一番はずっと変わらなかった。
…途中からだけど、ずっと彼を見てるわたしならわかる」
examples.todokanai: "Even so, I'll never be able to become the one he loves most. …I know because I've always watched him, even if not for as long as you."

examples.note: Kazusa says if Haruki happens to choose her she will count that day as lucky; 'every now and then' invents a request for periodic access.
examples.japanese:
「ただ、たまたまあたしを選んでくれたら、
今日はラッキーだったなって思うだけだ」
examples.todokanai: "As long as you pick me every now and then, I'll think of myself as lucky for that day."

examples.note: The English preserves the uncertain distance of the snow image without inventing a location or stronger causal claim.
examples.japanese:
二人が、同じ雪雲を見上げ…
遠い空の下のあいつにこの雪が届かない日にも。
examples.todokanai: Even during the days when we look up at those same snow-laden clouds… and she is somewhere so far away that the snow doesn't reach her.

examples.note: The open alternatives remain open: the event could happen tomorrow, in a year, or never.
examples.japanese:
「やっぱり明日かもしれないし一年後かもしれない。
もしかしたらそんなこと、一生起こらないかもしれない」
examples.todokanai: "It could be tomorrow, it could be a year from now. It might not even happen at all."

dossiers.title: Motive, culpability, and moral framing
dossiers.claim: Across all four sections, Todokanai TL repeatedly changes the moral grammar of an action: who knowingly chose it, whether the speaker is confessing a fault or merely suffering, and whether a motive is additive, conditional, retrospective, or self-exculpatory. These are not abstract disagreements about whether a character is good or bad. The Japanese explicitly supplies the agency and moral relation that the English changes.
dossiers.sourcePattern: Maruto's characters often prosecute themselves through repeated evaluative words, modal distinctions, and verbs of choosing, using, fleeing, enduring, or taking responsibility. A line's ethical force may depend on knowing versus ignoring, a retrospective 'what I have done' versus a future duty, or a confession that selfish desire existed in addition to an altruistic motive.
dossiers.todokanaiEffect: The mistranslations systematically alter the reader's case against the characters. Haruki's repeated self-condemnation becomes generalized bad behavior; ignorance becomes willful disregard; active instrumentalization becomes passive suffering; and Setsuna's admission of mixed motives becomes the much harsher claim that she acted only for herself. Across routes, the resulting English reallocates culpability rather than merely changing tone.
dossiers.limits: The dossier does not infer hidden motives, settle moral debates, or treat every naturalizing paraphrase as exculpation. Every red example turns on an explicit source distinction in agency, modality, time, or logical relation. The counterexamples show that Todokanai TL can preserve shared culpability and can preserve Haruki's benevolent-but-controlling conduct without forcing either side into a simpler moral category.

examples.note: Haruki repeats 最低 and turns his first betrayal into a self-imposed obligation to remain the worst. Todokanai TL replaces that repeated identity with plural 'despicable actions' and invents the moralizing claim that abandoning them 'wouldn't be right.'
examples.japanese:
一度、最低の裏切りをしてしまった相手だから。
もう、ずっと最低を貫かなくちゃならないから。
examples.todokanai: I've already committed the most despicable act of betrayal against her, after all. It wouldn't be right not to see my despicable actions to their very end.

examples.note: Haruki condemns himself as one person possessing both the coldness to exploit weakness and the baseness to ignore another's circumstances. The English generalizes this into advice about two kinds of “people,” softens 冷徹 into “cool-headed,” and turns 卑劣 into ordinary selfishness.
examples.japanese:
人の弱みに付け込む冷徹さと、
人の事情を考えない卑劣さを持つ人間を、
そんなに簡単に信じていいわけがないって。
examples.todokanai: You shouldn't easily believe in cool-headed people who take advantage of others' weaknesses, or selfish people who don't consider others' circumstances.

examples.note: Io says Haruki rushed ahead without knowing Setsuna's feelings. 'Ignored' means he knew them and willfully disregarded them, materially increasing his culpability and changing the information state on which he acted.
examples.japanese:
「春希が悪いんだから。
あいつが、雪菜の気持ちも知らずに先走って…」
examples.todokanai: "It's all Haruki's fault. He completely ignored your feelings and acted rashly, Setsuna…"

examples.note: Setsuna says there were many painful and difficult experiences at first, then separately apologizes for the awful things she said. The translation turns the suffering itself into painful and cruel acts she committed.
examples.japanese:
「色々とあったけど…
特に、最初は辛いことや苦しいことが多くて、
色々と酷いこと言っちゃってごめんなさい」
examples.todokanai: "So much has happened… Especially when it first started, there were so many painful and cruel things I did… And I also said so many awful things to you. For that, I'm sorry."

examples.note: Haruki says that this tangled history is nevertheless what he himself has done—the accumulated consequence of his choices. The English turns that retrospective ownership into a statement about what he must do next, replacing self-accounting with future obligation just before Koharu rejects his framing.
examples.japanese: 「でもそれが、自分のしてきたことだから…」
examples.todokanai: "But that's just what I have to do…"

examples.note: Haruki says that deciding unilaterally that one has paid the price is meaningless unless the other person changes. The translation instead requires the other person to accept the sacrifice, replacing a change in their state or behavior with approval.
examples.japanese:
「自分一人が落とし前をつけたって思ってても、
相手が変わってくれなかったら何の意味もない」
examples.todokanai: "Even if you think of paying the price alone, it will be meaningless if the other party doesn't accept it."

examples.note: Haruki actively recognizes that he is now running toward escape. The English says only that his resolve is leaving, removing his choice and culpability from the retreat.
examples.japanese:
たった数時間前の決意が、
たった一つの挫折でもろくも崩れ去り、
今はもう、逃避に走ろうとしてる。
examples.todokanai: The resolve I had from just a few hours ago is, with just a single setback that made it break apart, already on its way out the door.

examples.note: Haruki vows that he himself will support/carry two people—no, all three lives including Youko. The English redistributes the burden equally among the three, undoing Youko's warning that no one will support him.
examples.japanese:
「ちゃんと現地で仕事を探して、言葉も勉強して、
二人…いや、三人だって抱えてみせます」
examples.todokanai: "I'll make sure to find employment over there, I'll learn the necessary language, and the two of us… no, the three of us will bear it all together."

examples.note: Haruki says that otherwise there would have been no point in using so many people as stepping stones. The English replaces his ruthless, self-aware instrumentalization of others with the more passive suffering they caused.
examples.japanese: でないと、あれだけ多くの人を踏み台にした意味がない。
examples.todokanai: The amount of suffering we've caused to so many people would have been for nothing otherwise.

examples.note: Kazusa asks whether Setsuna believes restoring her is a way of devoting herself to Haruki—doing for him what he would do. 'Winning his favor' instead imputes a calculated attempt to ingratiate herself with him, materially changing Setsuna's motive and Kazusa's accusation.
examples.japanese:
「お前があたしに構うのは、あいつがそうするからだろ？
あたしを立ち直らせることが、
あいつに尽くすことだって思ってるんだろ？」
examples.todokanai: "The reason that you're concerned about me is because he himself is concerned about me, right? And you think you're winning his favor by trying to help me up on my feet again, don't you?"

examples.note: Setsuna says saving Haruki was not her only motive; she also wanted to satisfy her own desire. Todokanai TL turns the additive confession into an exclusive contrast—she did not act to save him, only for herself—making her self-accusation much harsher than the source.
examples.japanese:
彼を救いたいから、だけじゃない。
自分の欲望も満足させたかったから。
examples.todokanai: Not so I can save him, but to satisfy my own desires.

examples.note: The English preserves that Haruki and Kazusa both knew their earlier act was despicable and nevertheless did not stop. Shared knowledge and shared culpability survive without being reassigned to only one participant.
examples.japanese:
だって、五年前の俺たちも…
互いに『最悪のこと』ってわかってて、
それでも止まらなかっただけ、なんだから。
examples.todokanai: Because even five years ago… we both knew we were doing something despicable. We merely didn't stop in spite of that.

examples.note: The English retains both sides of Haruki's recurring conduct: he pays little attention to Setsuna's thoughts and forcibly concludes the exchange, yet does so by insisting that he will come for her again. The line remains controlling and caring at once.
examples.japanese:
「嫌かな？　俺と帰るの」

「っ、そんなことない」

「それとも、余計なお節介がウザいかな？」

「それがなくちゃ春希くんじゃない！」

「…褒め言葉と取っていいんだよな、それ」

「あ、ごめん…」

　形式的に謝ってはみたものの、雪菜は自分の台詞が失言だったなんてまるで思っていなかった。

　ついでに、そんな自分の認識が彼を貶めているという可能性を考えたことも…

「とにかく、雪菜！」

「は、はいっ？」

「俺、やっぱり明日も迎えに行くから！　絶対に待っててくれよな」

「え？　え？」

　と、考え事をしている雪菜をよそに、春希が強引にまとめに入る。
examples.todokanai:
“Do you not like going home with me, or something?”

“N-No, it’s not that—“

“Or is it annoying, having me insist on helping like this?”

“If you didn’t, you wouldn’t be you, Haruki-kun!”

“…Should I take that as a compliment?”

“Ah, sorry…”

Though she apologized as a matter of form, Setsuna didn’t see her words as a gaffe in the least.

Nor did it occur to her that her own awareness of the fact might come out as a show of contempt for him…

“Anyway, Setsuna!”

“Y-Yes?”

“I’m gonna come and get you tomorrow, too! So you’d better wait for me.”

“Huh? What?”

Taking little notice of Setsuna’s absorption in her own thoughts, Haruki brought things forcibly to a conclusion.

dossiers.title: Relationship roles, ranking, and the trio
dossiers.claim: Todokanai TL repeatedly changes the explicit topology of the central relationships: who loved whom, who possessed or relinquished a prior claim, whether two people became a couple or three became two through loss, and whether a ranking is present, past, equal, or impossible. In a work whose drama depends on unstable two-person and three-person structures, these are architectural errors.
dossiers.sourcePattern: The Japanese carefully marks referents, number, possession, temporal continuity, and comparison. Haruki can love Setsuna while choosing Kazusa; Setsuna can concede Kazusa's first claim while describing her own effort; and the trio can be an irreducible relationship rather than generic indecision. Repeated labels and adjacent replies often resolve any omitted subject.
dossiers.todokanaiEffect: The English turns continuing love into past love, equality into near-equality, a bond with two women into an indecisive life, and Kazusa's first claim into an unrelated statement about priorities. It can also grant romantic ownership where the source denies it or remove ownership where guilt depends on it. The broad plot remains recognizable while the relational logic governing guilt, jealousy, and choice changes underneath it.
dossiers.limits: The dossier does not impose a single thematic interpretation on ambiguous affection. It uses explicit referents, number, tense, possession, and stated comparison. The counterexamples demonstrate that Todokanai TL sometimes preserves both the structural impossibility of returning from three to two and the shared culpability of a relationship that crosses the boundary anyway.

examples.note: The Japanese pointedly gives Kazusa and Setsuna different marked labels: 'that one' leaves, while 'the girl and I' remain. Todokanai TL renders both women as the identical quoted 'she,' erasing the hierarchy and making the quotation marks meaningless.
examples.japanese:
『あいつ』は去った。
そして、『俺とあの娘』だけが残った。
examples.todokanai: "She" is gone now. And only "she and I" remain.

examples.note: Setsuna says she took Haruki and made him no longer Kazusa's, explicitly framing her act as theft from a prior claim. The English changes this to Kazusa's future inability to have him, weakening Setsuna's confession of guilt and the presupposed emotional ownership.
examples.japanese:
「わたし…春希くん取っちゃったんだよ？
冬馬さんのものじゃ、なくしちゃったんだよ？」
examples.todokanai: "I've taken Haruki-kun away, you know? You won't be able to have him for yourself, Touma-san, you know?"

examples.note: Haruki calls Setsuna someone as important to him as Mari, 同じくらい. 'Almost as important' creates a hierarchy absent from the confession and softens precisely the equality that makes the disclosure devastating.
examples.japanese: 「俺にとって、麻理さんと同じくらい大切な人の」
examples.todokanai: "She's someone important to me, almost as important as you are, Mari-san…"

examples.note: Haruki says he saw in Mari the traces of someone he once loved, and fell for Mari while simultaneously loving a person he still loves now. 今でも好きな人 modifies the other person, not Mari. The English attaches the continuing love to Mari and reverses the temporal/referential structure of his divided heart.
examples.japanese:
「俺は麻理さんに、昔好きだった人の面影を見てた。
麻理さんを、今でも好きな人と同時に好きになった」
examples.todokanai: "I see someone I used to be in love with in Mari-san. And I'm in love with someone else simultaneously, even though I'm still in love with Mari-san right now."

examples.note: Haruki answers in the present: he loves Setsuna and has remained in love with her. The English changes both clauses to past love, erasing the deliberately cruel paradox that he still loves her while choosing someone else.
examples.japanese:
「好きだよ…
ずっと、好きなままだよ…っ」
examples.todokanai: "Of course I loved you… I've always loved you all this time…"

examples.note: Kazusa warns Haruki about abandoning the person he has loved continuously for five years: Setsuna. The translation makes Setsuna the one who has loved Haruki, reversing the subject and weakening Kazusa's insistence that his own love remains.
examples.japanese:
「だから、そんなことしてしまったら…
五年間もずっと愛してきた相手を捨ててしまったら…
お前、一生後悔して生きていくことになるんだぞ？」
examples.todokanai: "If you do this… If you abandon the person who has loved you so earnestly for five years, you'll regret it for the rest of your life."

examples.note: Haruki says this would not be a life of mere indecision; it would be a life deeply bound to both women. The English calls him indecisive, erasing the distinction that explains why the arrangement would injure both.
examples.japanese:
そんな、どっちつかずでもない、
どっちとも深く繋がってしまう人生は、
俺の世界で一番大切な二人を不幸にしてしまう。
examples.todokanai: I'd only end up making the two people I care about more than anyone else in the world completely miserable, chaining them to myself in a limbo where I'm closely tied to the both of them, yet also indecisive at the same time.

examples.note: Kazusa says Haruki liked Setsuna five years ago and that she knows because she watched him. 'You're the one he's truly loved' adds both singular 'the one' and 'truly,' suggesting an exclusivity the source does not state before the following discussion of who remained number one.
examples.japanese:
「あいつは五年前から雪菜のことが好きだったよ。
ずっとあいつを見てたあたしだからわかるんだよ…」
examples.todokanai: "You're the one he's truly loved since five years ago, Setsuna. I know that full well because I've been watching him all that time…"

examples.note: Setsuna says Haruki's number one had remained unchanged throughout that period. The English turns this retrospective observation into a permanent prediction that she will never become number one, immediately clashing with her next statement that her best was to draw level and Kazusa's answer that Setsuna ultimately did become the woman he loves most.
examples.japanese:
「それでも、彼の中の一番はずっと変わらなかった。
…途中からだけど、ずっと彼を見てるわたしならわかる」
examples.todokanai: "Even so, I'll never be able to become the one he loves most. …I know because I've always watched him, even if not for as long as you."

examples.note: Setsuna confesses the contradiction plainly: while asking the other two to preserve the trio, she herself sought to be alone with Haruki. The first translated sentence is nonsensical and duplicates the second instead of stating what she demanded of Haruki and Kazusa.
examples.japanese:
「三人でいることを二人に求めておきながら、
自分は彼と二人になることを求めた。
…かずさのこと、出し抜いた」
examples.todokanai: "I sought to become two amongst the three of us… I wanted to become two with him. …And I ended up stealing the march on you, Kazusa."

examples.note: Haruki is the person whom only Kazusa had been looking at from the beginning, which Setsuna uses to grant Kazusa first claim. Todokanai TL reverses the gaze into Haruki looking at Kazusa, then mistranslates Kazusa's 優先権—priority or first claim—as her having 'her own priorities.'
examples.japanese:
――わたしは三人でいられるならいいんだ。

　　ううん、それこそがわたしが本当に望んだことなんだ。

　　だから…冬馬さんが春希くんとつきあっても、大丈夫なんだ。

　　もともと、冬馬さんだけが見ていたひとなんだもん。

　　あのコに優先権があるんだもん。

　　わたしがどれだけ割り込もうとしたって、勝てない絆があるもん。

　　だから、だから…

I’m okay with us staying a trio.

No, that’s actually exactly what I want.

So… it’s okay if Touma-san dates Haruki-kun.

He’s been looking at her this whole time, anyway.

She has her own priorities.

No matter how I might try to wedge myself in, that’s not a bond I can win against.

So… So…

examples.note: Todokanai TL preserves the structural cost of accepting the trio: once all three are admitted, Haruki can no longer return to a two-person relationship with either woman.
examples.japanese:
それでも無理やり三人でいることを選んだら、
二度と二人に戻ることができなくなってしまう。
examples.todokanai: Even so, if I were to force myself to accept the three of us being together, I won't be able to return to just the two of us ever again.

examples.note: The English preserves Haruki and Kazusa as joint participants who both knew the act was despicable and did not stop. It does not simplify the relationship violation into unilateral victimhood or unilateral guilt.
examples.japanese:
だって、五年前の俺たちも…
互いに『最悪のこと』ってわかってて、
それでも止まらなかっただけ、なんだから。
examples.todokanai: Because even five years ago… we both knew we were doing something despicable. We merely didn't stop in spite of that.

dossiers.title: Psychological focalization and emotional subject
dossiers.claim: Todokanai TL often preserves a plausible emotion while moving it into the wrong mind. Relief, shame, temptation, pain, knowledge, and concealment are reassigned between observer and observed, speaker and listener, or Haruki and one of the women. The sentence may remain fluent in isolation while the scene's psychology becomes false.
dossiers.sourcePattern: The narration frequently embeds one character's inference about another inside first-person focalization. Omitted Japanese subjects are resolved by possessives, continuing thought sequences, visible expressions, and the action that follows. Maruto also distinguishes an emotion itself from one character's reading of that emotion, and a private conclusion from insight into somebody else's heart.
dossiers.todokanaiEffect: A lonely smile becomes an instrument that reads Haruki's heart; Setsuna's relief is assigned to Haruki; Haruki's awareness of temptation is assigned to Setsuna; and deliberate emotional concealment becomes accidental invisibility. Because the substituted emotion is usually scene-plausible, these errors can survive casual reading while reversing who understands, wounds, reassures, or hides from whom.
dossiers.limits: Free-indirect ambiguity is not treated as an error merely because another reading is possible. The selected findings require local grammatical or sequential evidence that resolves the experiencer or focalizer. The counterexamples show Todokanai TL preserving opposed emotional shocks and preserving Kazusa's frightening long-horizon calculation without flattening either into generic sadness.

examples.note: While Haruki hesitates, Setsuna stands looking relieved—perhaps because having her identity exposed has cleared the air. The English invents her noticing his hesitation and makes that the focus of her expression.
examples.japanese:
そんなふうに逡巡してる隙に、
小木曽は正体がバレてスッキリしてしまったのか、
結構晴れ晴れとした顔で立ち上がる。
examples.todokanai: Ogiso gives me a cheerful look, making me wonder whether she'd noticed I was hesitating just now.

examples.note: Kazusa insists there is no way she is not happy to be with Haruki and Setsuna. The English abruptly puts the final and most vulnerable admission in the past, making it possible to read her happiness as something already over rather than an ongoing feeling she is struggling to voice.
examples.japanese:
『………嫌なわけないだろ。
楽しくないわけないだろ。
嬉しくないわけないだろ』
examples.todokanai: "…There's no way I wouldn't like it. There's no way it wouldn't be fun. There's no way I wasn't happy."

examples.note: Setsuna's lonely smile is transparent enough that her own true feelings show through it. The English makes Setsuna's smile see through Haruki's heart, reversing whose inner state is exposed and who perceives it.
examples.japanese:
俺のために、俺の目の前でいつでも笑ってた。
本当の心が透けて見えるくらいに、
寂しい笑顔で笑ってた。
examples.todokanai: She continued to force herself to smile for me. I felt as if she could see straight through my heart with her lonesome smile.

examples.note: Setsuna's warm, foolish feelings gouge Haruki's heart in his narration. The translation makes those feelings wound Setsuna's own heart, reversing the emotional impact at the center of his self-indictment.
examples.japanese: 雪菜の温かくて愚かな気持ちが、心を抉る。
examples.todokanai: That caused Setsuna's own tender but foolish feelings to stab at her heart.

examples.note: Haruki resolves to be gentle so that, when morning comes, Setsuna can feel relief from the bottom of her heart and smile, believing the path she chose was right. The English assigns the reassurance and smile to Haruki himself, reversing the object of his concern.
examples.japanese:
朝を迎えたとき、自分の選んだ道が正しかったって、
心の底から安心して、微笑んでもらえるように。
examples.todokanai: Once morning comes, I want to smile and take comfort in knowing that the path I chose was the right one.

examples.note: Haruki says he himself was conscious that this was devilish temptation. The translation assigns the awareness to Setsuna and weakens it into speculation.
examples.japanese: 悪魔の誘惑だって、自覚してた。
examples.todokanai: She must have become aware of the devilish temptation we're locked in.

examples.note: Haruki thinks Setsuna noticed his own improper thought that her jealous face was cute. The translation says Setsuna realizes her own undignified behavior, reversing whose impropriety she detects.
examples.japanese:
なんて、やっぱりその不謹慎に勘付かれたか、
大きな足音を立てて二階へ上がってしまった
雪菜が…つまりさっきまでそこにいた。
examples.todokanai: Perhaps in realization of her own undignified behavior, Setsuna stomped her way to the second floor. Which meant that Setsuna… saw our exchange up until a moment ago.

examples.note: Koharu says that even if Haruki is content to leave, she is not, because abandoning him would be bad for her own peace of mind. The English instead comments on Haruki's mental state, removing Koharu's explicit reason for chasing and caring for him.
examples.japanese:
「先輩はよくてもわたしがよくないんです！
精神衛生上！」
examples.todokanai: "You might think you're alright, but to me, you're not! In terms of your mental state, that is!"

examples.note: Haruki says he had considered the possibility that Setsuna already knew but lacked confirmation until seconds ago. The translation assigns the suspicions and lack of proof to Setsuna, reversing the focalized knower.
examples.japanese:
その可能性に、まるで思い至らない訳じゃなかった。
ただ、ずっと確証が持てなかった。
………ほんの数秒前までは。
examples.todokanai: She probably had her suspicions of what was happening, she just never had any positive proof… up until these last few seconds.

examples.note: Words denying Setsuna's self-condemnation rise one after another in Haruki's mind, and he crushes each one before speaking it. The English makes Setsuna's words invade and damage him, erasing his deliberate silence.
examples.japanese:
否定の言葉が、次から次へと頭の中に浮かび、
そして、次から次へと頭の中で潰していく。
examples.todokanai: One after another, her words enter my head, and one after another, they wreak havoc.

examples.note: Setsuna has deliberately stopped letting Io see her present expression; the English says only that Io happens to be unable to see her face, removing Setsuna's act of emotional concealment.
examples.japanese:
「みんな～、早く早く！　昼間のサービスタイムは六時までなんだからね～！」

　そして雪菜は、そのまま依緒を置いてきぼりにしてさっさと足を速める。

「って、何時間歌うつもりなんだよ…」

　やっと突っ込みどころを見つけてぽつりと呟いたとき、雪菜はもう今の表情を依緒には見せてはくれなかった。

　たった一月で、雪菜は微妙に変わった。

　今まで以上に壁が取り払われた気がした。例を挙げれば、少しお喋りになった、少し意地悪になった、少しお節介になった、そしていつも笑うようになった。

「雪菜、お前はさ…」

　もう、その小さな呟きが相手に届かないことを知りつつ、依緒はあえて続けた。

“Come on, guys, hurry up! The daytime discount only lasts until six!”

And Setsuna left her there, quickening her steps.

“Hang on, how many hours are you planning to sing…?”

By the time Io managed to mutter a retort, Setsuna was no longer looking at her. She couldn’t see her face.

In only a month, Setsuna had undergone a subtle change.

More of her walls seemed to have been demolished now. To give a few examples, she was a little chattier, a little meaner, a little nosier, and she smiled all the time.

“Setsuna, you…”

Io knew that her muttering wouldn’t reach her target’s ears, but she continued anyway.

examples.japanese:
そんな麻理さんの言葉は、
まったく逆方向からの二つの衝撃を、
俺にもたらした。
examples.todokanai: Mari-san's words strike me hard from two opposite directions.

examples.note: Todokanai TL retains Kazusa's precise and terrifying emotional arithmetic: five years apart became nearly nothing, so even ten years might be overcome.
examples.japanese:
俺たちの間の五年なんて、ないも同然だった…
十年なら、平気で乗り越えてしまうかもしれない。
examples.todokanai: These past five years apart might as well not have happened… We might actually be able to overcome ten years with ease.

dossiers.title: Body blocking, physical action, and consent
dossiers.claim: Across romantic, sexual, and nonsexual scenes, Todokanai TL repeatedly changes who moves, the direction and force of contact, or the bodily terms under which contact is offered. These are scene-blocking errors: they alter what the characters physically do before any interpretation of the act begins.
dossiers.sourcePattern: The Japanese often stages emotion through paired bodily alternatives, explicit body parts, directional verbs, posture, and quoted requests that define the force or route of contact. It also distinguishes enacted contact from hypothetical possibility and physical constraint from emotional reluctance.
dossiers.todokanaiEffect: A kiss initiated by Haruki becomes one initiated by Setsuna; reduced force becomes greater force; legs already opened around Haruki become legs closing to escape; kneeling becomes standing; and concrete pinning and groping become hypothetical possibilities. The changed blocking can reverse initiative, manufacture resistance, erase consent terms, or delete a deliberate visual parallel.
dossiers.limits: This dossier is descriptive rather than exculpatory: accurate blocking does not imply ethical approval, and consent is never inferred from silence. Findings require explicit movement, body position, force, or quoted permission. The counterexamples show a public/private restraint rule and a final decision left explicitly to Haruki, both preserved without inventing physical action.

examples.note: After Setsuna finally pulls her lips away when Haruki's arms loosen, he realizes retrospectively that he had been the one pressing the kiss onto her. Todokanai TL invents a new second advance after the separation—“once more”—materially changing the physical sequence and sexual agency.

examples.todokanai: …And then, I force myself onto Setsuna once more.

examples.note: This touch lacks Chiaki's usual forcefulness—the rough play that normally spares Haruki embarrassment by keeping contact unserious. The English says her grip is stronger, reversing the tactile change that makes the gentle contact more intimate.
examples.japanese:
いつもの力強さ...って言うか、
俺の照れと躊躇を誘発しないための気遣いがない。
examples.todokanai: Her grip is stronger than it usually is… perhaps she's just not bothering to make sure I'm not embarrassed or hesitant this time.

examples.note: Setsuna explicitly asks Haruki to do it forcefully, not take detours, and come to her quickly. The translation substitutes making a mess and not holding back, obscuring the force and direct-route instructions that define the requested act.
examples.japanese:
「無理やり、して。
寄り道なんかしないで。
早く、わたしのところに来てよぉ」
examples.todokanai: "Make a mess of me. Don't hold back. Hurry up and come to me already."

examples.japanese:
ドアを閉めた途端、強引に抱きしめ唇を重ねると、
あっという間に甘い吐息とともに目を閉じて、

examples.todokanai: Before the door even closed, she forcefully hugged me and pressed her lips against mine. Shutting her eyes as she let out her sweet breath after a few moments, she slowly surrendered herself to me.

一生懸命にぴんと張られる。
examples.todokanai: As if trying to escape from me, she desperately tries to close her legs which I'd pried open.

examples.note: The source explicitly pairs mind/heart with body. 'Heart and soul' duplicates the psychological half and erases bodily injury from Haruki's guilt after the sexual relationship.
examples.japanese:
それなのに…
心も身体も、ボロボロに傷つけられたはずなのに…
examples.todokanai: And yet… even though her heart and soul should be heavily wounded by all that…

Repeated 'I could' wording turns the enacted assaultive contact into a hypothetical possibility.

強く押し倒し、全身でのしかかって拘束し、
激しくその身体をまさぐっても。

　数分後…

　学園祭の喧騒から唯一忘れ去られたかのような第二音楽室。

「春希、くん…」

　先ほどのかずさと同じ体勢で、春希の前にかしずく雪菜の姿がそこにあった。

　窓から、最後の夕陽のかけらが弱々しく入り込んでいる。

　けれど多分、あと十分もしないうちにその灯りも消え、その存在は闇に葬られるに違いない。

A few minutes later…

In Music Room #2, which alone seemed to have been completely forgotten in the excitement of the school festival…

“Haruki-kun…”

Setsuna stood waiting in front of Haruki, in the same posture Kazusa had taken a short while earlier.

The last rays of the setting sun shone weakly in through the window.

But, in all likelihood, that glow would vanish within the next ten minutes, its existence buried in darkness.

だって、外だから…
誰かに見られるかもしれないからこそ、
俺はこうして、かずさに触れられる。
examples.todokanai: Because we're outside… It's precisely because there's a chance someone might see us that I can touch Kazusa like this.

examples.todokanai: "The rest is up to you."

dossiers.title: Sexual action, intimacy, and event detail
dossiers.claim: Todokanai TL repeatedly changes the literal mechanics of explicit scenes: who initiates or performs an act, which body part is involved, where fluid is located, and whether the Japanese describes intercourse, oral contact, or an embrace. The errors are neither prudish complaints nor demands for anatomical excess; they change events and characterization.
dossiers.sourcePattern: The source uses direct verbs, agent-patient relations, body locations, and completed-action context even when the surrounding narration is emotionally figurative. It also uses 抱く and 抱きしめる in context-sensitive ways, sometimes sexual and sometimes literally an embrace whose hold/let-go imagery is load-bearing.
dossiers.todokanaiEffect: The English reverses pursuit, changes oral sex into clutching, turns unidentified white fluid drawn from inside Setsuna into newly ejaculated semen, transfers undressing between partners, moves semen from an abdomen to inside the body, and replaces literal penetration with metaphorical sobs. Elsewhere it invents sex where the source says embrace, destroying a deliberate hierarchy of first acts or a hold/let-go parallel.
dossiers.limits: The dossier includes only sexual meanings established by immediate grammar and scene continuity. It does not expand euphemism into unsupported anatomy, and it treats embrace as sex only where the source and context do. The counterexamples show explicit escalation and mutual continuation preserved directly, demonstrating that accurate sexual translation need not be either sanitized or embellished.

examples.note: Io says the man is desperately trying to win the woman's attention, and if she likes him she should let him take her to bed or embrace her. The translation makes the woman desperate and tells her to initiate the embrace, reversing both pursuit and sexual agency.

そいつに気があるなら女は抱かれてあげるんだよ」
examples.todokanai: "If you want a man to show you affection, you have to take some desperate measures. If you're interested in him, go embrace him, girl."

examples.note: Setsuna ravenously fastens her mouth onto Haruki's penis. The translation substitutes clutching it, changing the body part and sexual act.
examples.japanese:
こんな扇情的な言葉まで駆使して、
俺のものにむしゃぶりつく。
examples.todokanai: She's freely making use of such lascivious words and clutching my thing.

examples.note: White viscous fluid is drawn or scraped out from Setsuna by Haruki's penis and drips onto the bed. The translation identifies it as semen ejaculated from his penis, reversing its source and motion.
examples.japanese:
俺のに掻き出されてきたように、
白い粘液が、とろりと流れ落ちて、
